entry.title: A $12,100 budget, a telephone outreach and a retreat with the university president
entry.body: ASG approved an operating budget of $12,100. It also planned a telephone outreach effort to hear students' ideas and needs, and announced a retreat featuring university president Kern Alexander. The Herald carried all three items on 11 September 1986, in the second week of the fall semester.

entry.title: Two voucher bills pass unanimously, a poetry night by one vote short of it
entry.body: Bill 28-23-S put $500 toward free teeth cleanings at the WKU Dental Health Clinic, amended by committee chair Adan Canizalez to draw on the scholarship programme fund rather than the Legislative Discretionary Fund. Chief of staff Lauren Willett, an author of the bill, said voucher use had risen 660 per cent over the fall semester. Bill 27-23-S allocated $2,000 split 60/30/10 between the ID centre, the Preston Center and the dental hygiene clinic, and both bills passed unanimously. A third bill, $260 for a poetry mic night run with the Talisman, passed on a roll call with senator Ethan Huffaker the only vote against, citing superfluous spending; former SGA president Matthew Wininger had opened the meeting as guest speaker.

entry.title: Regents raise tuition over the student regent's lone no vote
entry.body: The Board of Regents approved a $204 tuition increase, of 1.69 per cent, taking tuition to $6,240 a semester, the sixth consecutive yearly rise, alongside a 5 per cent housing increase and a 2 per cent meal plan increase within a $405 million operating budget. Every regent voted for it except outgoing SGA president Rush Robinson, who said the board had to do everything it could to preserve affordability. It was his last meeting as student regent before Caden Lucas took the seat. The board also suspended several majors, kinesiology and geological sciences among them, for reworking and mergers.

Spring Fling funding passes 28-2 after cost objections

entry.title: Four bills fund a month of events, and one of them takes a fight
entry.body: At the 23rd Senate's twentieth meeting, on 12 March 2024, four funding bills passed. Bill 34-23-S gave $150 to an SGA Diversity, Equity and Inclusion week of tabling from 25 to 28 March, a different initiative each day: mental health, campus demographics, safe sexual health, and deaf awareness. Bill 35-23-S gave $450 to an SGA Spring Fling on the South Lawn, a cookout with kickball and cornhole tournaments and raffles for Uber vouchers, its proceeds going to the Kids Cancer Alliance; after debate among senators over the amount it passed 28-2, the only bill of the four not carried unanimously. Bill 36-23-S gave $280 to a Hope Harbor Denim Day event on sexual assault awareness and Bill 38-23-S gave $650 to the annual Mental Health Week in April.
